title: Conditional mutual information bounded by conditional entropy
statement:
Let $X$, $Y$, and $Z$ be measurable random variables on a common probability space $(\Omega, \mu)$, each taking values in a countable measurable space and each having finite range, and suppose $\mu$ is either the zero measure or a probability measure. Then the conditional mutual information of $X$ and $Y$ given $Z$ is at most the conditional entropy of $Y$ given $Z$:
\[
  I[X : Y \mid Z ; \mu] \;\le\; H[Y \mid Z ; \mu].
\]
hypotheses_covered: values in countable spaces with singletons measurable
X, Y, Z have finite range
mu is zero or a probability measure
replaced:
For measurable $X$, $Y$, $Z$ under a zero-or-probability measure with finite ranges,
\[
  I[X : Y \mid Z;\mu] \;\le\; H[Y \mid Z;\mu].
\]
